5501   /**
5502    * Parses a number from the specified string.
5503    *
5504    * <p>
5505    * Supports Java 7+ numeric literals with underscores (e.g., <js>"1_000_000"</js>).
5506    * The underscores are automatically removed before parsing.
5507    *
5508    * @param s The string to parse the number from.
5509    * @param type
5510    *    The number type to created.
5511    *    Can be any of the following:
5512    *    <ul>
5513    *       <li> Integer (or <c>int</c> primitive)
5514    *       <li> Long (or <c>long</c> primitive)
5515    *       <li> Short (or <c>short</c> primitive)
5516    *       <li> Byte (or <c>byte</c> primitive)
5517    *       <li> Float (or <c>float</c> primitive)
5518    *       <li> Double (or <c>double</c> primitive)
5519    *       <li> BigInteger
5520    *       <li> BigDecimal
5521    *       <li> AtomicInteger
5522    *       <li> AtomicLong
5523    *    </ul>
5524    *    If <jk>null</jk> or <c>Number</c>, uses the best guess.
5525    * @return The parsed number, or <jk>null</jk> if the string was null.
5526    */
5527   public static Number parseNumber(String s, Class<? extends Number> type) {
5528      if (s == null)
5529         return null;
5530      if (s.isEmpty())
5531         s = "0";
5532      if (type == null)
5533         type = Number.class;
5534
5535      // Remove underscores (Java 7+ numeric literal support) before parsing
5536      // Note: We do this before type detection to ensure clean parsing
5537      s = s.replace("_", "");
5538
5539      // Determine the data type if it wasn't specified.
5540      var isAutoDetect = (type == Number.class);
5541      var isDecimal = false;
5542      if (isAutoDetect) {
5543         // If we're auto-detecting, then we use either an Integer, Long, or Double depending on how
5544         // long the string is.
5545         // An integer range is -2,147,483,648 to 2,147,483,647
5546         // An long range is -9,223,372,036,854,775,808 to +9,223,372,036,854,775,807
5547         isDecimal = isDecimal(s);
5548         if (isDecimal) {
5549            if (s.length() > 20)
5550               type = Double.class;
5551            else if (s.length() >= 10)
5552               type = Long.class;
5553            else
5554               type = Integer.class;
5555         } else if (isFloat(s))
5556            type = Double.class;
5557         else
5558            throw new NumberFormatException(s);
5559      }
5560
5561      if (type == Double.class || type == Double.TYPE) {
5562         return Double.valueOf(s);
5563      }
5564      if (type == Float.class || type == Float.TYPE)
5565         return Float.valueOf(s);
5566      if (type == BigDecimal.class)
5567         return new BigDecimal(s);
5568      if (type == Long.class || type == Long.TYPE || type == AtomicLong.class) {
5569         try {
5570            var l = parseLongWithSuffix(s);
5571            if (type == AtomicLong.class)
5572               return new AtomicLong(l);
5573            if (isAutoDetect && l >= Integer.MIN_VALUE && l <= Integer.MAX_VALUE) {
5574               // This occurs if the string is 10 characters long but is still a valid integer value.
5575               return (int)l;
5576            }
5577            return l;
5578         } catch (NumberFormatException e) {
5579            if (isAutoDetect) {
5580               // This occurs if the string is 20 characters long but still falls outside the range of a valid long.
5581               return Double.valueOf(s);
5582            }
5583            throw e;
5584         }
5585      }
5586      if (type == Integer.class || type == Integer.TYPE)
5587         return Integer.decode(s);
5588      if (type == Short.class || type == Short.TYPE)
5589         return Short.decode(s);
5590      if (type == Byte.class || type == Byte.TYPE)
5591         return Byte.decode(s);
5592      if (type == BigInteger.class)
5593         return new BigInteger(s);
5594      if (type == AtomicInteger.class)
5595         return new AtomicInteger(Integer.decode(s));
5596      throw new NumberFormatException("Unsupported Number type: " + type.getName());
5597   }

5599   /**
5600    * Converts a string to PascalCase format.
5601    *
5602    * <p>
5603    * Handles various input formats:
5604    * <ul>
5605    *   <li>Space-separated: "hello world" → "HelloWorld"</li>
5606    *   <li>CamelCase: "helloWorld" → "HelloWorld"</li>
5607    *   <li>Snake_case: "hello_world" → "HelloWorld"</li>
5608    *   <li>Kebab-case: "hello-world" → "HelloWorld"</li>
5609    * </ul>
5610    *
5611    * <h5 class='section'>Example:</h5>
5612    * <p class='bjava'>
5613    *    pascalCase(<jk>null</jk>);                    <jc>// null</jc>
5614    *    pascalCase(<js>""</js>);                      <jc>// ""</jc>
5615    *    pascalCase(<js>"hello world"</js>);           <jc>// "HelloWorld"</jc>
5616    *    pascalCase(<js>"helloWorld"</js>);            <jc>// "HelloWorld"</jc>
5617    *    pascalCase(<js>"hello_world"</js>);           <jc>// "HelloWorld"</jc>
5618    *    pascalCase(<js>"hello-world"</js>);           <jc>// "HelloWorld"</jc>
5619    * </p>
5620    *
5621    * @param str The string to convert.
5622    * @return The PascalCase string, or <jk>null</jk> if input is <jk>null</jk>.
5623    */
5624   public static String pascalCase(String str) {
5625      if (isEmpty(str))
5626         return str;
5627
5628      var words = splitWords(str);
5629      if (words.isEmpty())
5630         return "";
5631
5632      var result = new StringBuilder();
5633      for (var word : words) {
5634         result.append(capitalize(lowerCaseRoot(word)));
5635      }
5636
5637      return result.toString();
5638   }

5640   /**
5641    * Pluralizes a word based on a count.
5642    *
5643    * <p>
5644    * Simple pluralization that adds "s" to most words, with basic rules for words ending in "s", "x", "z", "ch", "sh" (add "es"),
5645    * and words ending in "y" preceded by a consonant (replace "y" with "ies").
5646    *
5647    * <h5 class='section'>Example:</h5>
5648    * <p class='bjava'>
5649    *    pluralize(<js>"cat"</js>, <js>1</js>);        <jc>// "cat"</jc>
5650    *    pluralize(<js>"cat"</js>, <js>2</js>);        <jc>// "cats"</jc>
5651    *    pluralize(<js>"box"</js>, <js>2</js>);        <jc>// "boxes"</jc>
5652    *    pluralize(<js>"city"</js>, <js>2</js>);       <jc>// "cities"</jc>
5653    * </p>
5654    *
5655    * @param word The word to pluralize.  Can be <jk>null</jk> (returned as-is).
5656    * @param count The count to determine if pluralization is needed.
5657    * @return The pluralized word if count is not 1, otherwise the original word.
5658    */
5659   public static String pluralize(String word, int count) {
5660      if (word == null || word.isEmpty())
5661         return word;
5662      if (count == 1)
5663         return word;
5664
5665      var lower = lowerCaseRoot(word);
5666      var length = word.length();
5667
5668      // Words ending in s, x, z, ch, sh -> add "es"
5669      if (lower.endsWith("s") || lower.endsWith("x") || lower.endsWith("z") || lower.endsWith("ch") || lower.endsWith("sh")) {
5670         return word + "es";
5671      }
5672
5673      // Words ending in "y" preceded by a consonant -> replace "y" with "ies"
5674      if (length > 1 && lower.endsWith("y")) {
5675         var secondLast = lower.charAt(length - 2);
5676         if (! VOWEL.contains(secondLast)) {
5677            return word.substring(0, length - 1) + "ies";
5678         }
5679      }
5680
5681      // Words ending in "f" or "fe" -> replace with "ves" (basic rule)
5682      if (lower.endsWith("f")) {
5683         return word.substring(0, length - 1) + "ves";
5684      }
5685      if (lower.endsWith("fe")) {
5686         return word.substring(0, length - 2) + "ves";
5687      }
5688
5689      // Default: add "s"
5690      return word + "s";
5691   }

5693   /**
5694    * Generated a random UUID with the specified number of characters.
5695    *
5696    * <p>
5697    * Characters are composed of lower-case ASCII letters and numbers only.
5698    *
5699    * <p>
5700    * This method conforms to the restrictions for hostnames as specified in <a class="doclink" href="https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc952">RFC 952</a>
5701    * Since each character has 36 possible values, the square approximation formula for the number of generated IDs
5702    * that would produce a 50% chance of collision is:
5703    * <c>sqrt(36^N)</c>.
5704    * Dividing this number by 10 gives you an approximation of the number of generated IDs needed to produce a
5705    * &lt;1% chance of collision.
5706    *
5707    * <p>
5708    * For example, given 5 characters, the number of generated IDs need to produce a &lt;1% chance of collision would
5709    * be:
5710    * <c>sqrt(36^5)/10=777</c>
5711    *
5712    * @param numchars The number of characters in the generated UUID.
5713    * @return A new random UUID.
5714    */
5715   public static String random(int numchars) {
5716      var sb = new StringBuilder(numchars);
5717      for (var i = 0; i < numchars; i++) {
5718         var c = RANDOM.nextInt(36) + 97;
5719         if (c > 'z')
5720            c -= ('z' - '0' + 1);
5721         sb.append((char)c);
5722      }
5723      return sb.toString();
5724   }

5726   /**
5727    * Generates a random alphabetic string of the specified length.
5728    *
5729    * <p>
5730    * Characters are composed of upper-case and lower-case ASCII letters (a-z, A-Z).
5731    *
5732    * <h5 class='section'>Example:</h5>
5733    * <p class='bjava'>
5734    *    randomAlphabetic(<jk>5</jk>);  <jc>// "aBcDe"</jc>
5735    * </p>
5736    *
5737    * @param length The length of the generated string.
5738    * @return A new random alphabetic string.
5739    */
5740   public static String randomAlphabetic(int length) {
5741      if (length < 0)
5742         throw iaex("Length must be non-negative: " + length);
5743      var sb = new StringBuilder(length);
5744      for (var i = 0; i < length; i++) {
5745         var c = RANDOM.nextInt(52);
5746         if (c < 26)
5747            sb.append((char)('a' + c));
5748         else
5749            sb.append((char)('A' + c - 26));
5750      }
5751      return sb.toString();
5752   }

5754   /**
5755    * Generates a random alphanumeric string of the specified length.
5756    *
5757    * <p>
5758    * Characters are composed of upper-case and lower-case ASCII letters and digits (a-z, A-Z, 0-9).
5759    *
5760    * <h5 class='section'>Example:</h5>
5761    * <p class='bjava'>
5762    *    randomAlphanumeric(<jk>8</jk>);  <jc>// "aB3dE5fG"</jc>
5763    * </p>
5764    *
5765    * @param length The length of the generated string.
5766    * @return A new random alphanumeric string.
5767    */
5768   public static String randomAlphanumeric(int length) {
5769      if (length < 0)
5770         throw iaex("Length must be non-negative: " + length);
5771      var sb = new StringBuilder(length);
5772      for (var i = 0; i < length; i++) {
5773         var c = RANDOM.nextInt(62);
5774         if (c < 10)
5775            sb.append((char)('0' + c));
5776         else if (c < 36)
5777            sb.append((char)('a' + c - 10));
5778         else
5779            sb.append((char)('A' + c - 36));
5780      }
5781      return sb.toString();
5782   }

5838    * <h5 class='section'>Example:</h5>
5839    * <p class='bjava'>
5840    *    randomString(<jk>5</jk>, <js>"ABC"</js>);  <jc>// "BACAB"</jc>
5841    * </p>
5842    *
5843    * @param length The length of the generated string.
5844    * @param chars The character set to use. Must not be null or empty.
5845    * @return A new random string.
5846    * @throws IllegalArgumentException If chars is null or empty, or length is negative.
5847    */
5848   public static String randomString(int length, String chars) {
5849      if (length < 0)
5850         throw iaex("Length must be non-negative: " + length);
5851      if (chars == null || chars.isEmpty())
5852         throw iaex("Character set must not be null or empty");
5853      var sb = new StringBuilder(length);
5854      var charsLen = chars.length();
5855      for (var i = 0; i < length; i++) {
5856         sb.append(chars.charAt(RANDOM.nextInt(charsLen)));
5857      }
5858      return sb.toString();
5859   }

5861   /**
5862    * Calculates a simple readability score for a string.
5863    *
5864    * <p>
5865    * Uses a simplified Flesch Reading Ease-like formula based on:
5866    * <ul>
5867    *   <li>Average words per sentence</li>
5868    *   <li>Average syllables per word (estimated)</li>
5869    * </ul>
5870    * Returns a score from 0-100, where higher scores indicate easier reading.
5871    *
5872    * <h5 class='section'>Example:</h5>
5873    * <p class='bjava'>
5874    *    readabilityScore(<js>"The cat sat."</js>);      <jc>// Higher score (simple)</jc>
5875    *    readabilityScore(<js>"The sophisticated..."</js>); <jc>// Lower score (complex)</jc>
5876    * </p>
5877    *
5878    * @param str The string to analyze. Can be <jk>null</jk>.
5879    * @return A readability score from 0-100, or <c>0.0</c> if the string is <jk>null</jk> or empty.
5880    */
5881   public static double readabilityScore(String str) {
5882      if (isEmpty(str))
5883         return 0.0;
5884
5885      var words = extractWords(str);
5886      if (words.isEmpty())
5887         return 0.0;
5888
5889      // Count sentences (ending with . ! ?)
5890      var sentenceCount = 0;
5891      for (var i = 0; i < str.length(); i++) {
5892         var c = str.charAt(i);
5893         if (c == '.' || c == '!' || c == '?') {
5894            sentenceCount++;
5895         }
5896      }
5897      if (sentenceCount == 0)
5898         sentenceCount = 1; // At least one sentence
5899
5900      // Calculate average words per sentence
5901      var avgWordsPerSentence = (double)words.size() / sentenceCount;
5902
5903      // Estimate average syllables per word (simplified: count vowel groups)
5904      var totalSyllables = 0;
5905      for (var word : words) {
5906         totalSyllables += estimateSyllables(word);
5907      }
5908      var avgSyllablesPerWord = (double)totalSyllables / words.size();
5909
5910      // Simplified Flesch Reading Ease formula
5911      // Score = 206.835 - (1.015 * ASL) - (84.6 * ASW)
5912      // Where ASL = average sentence length (words), ASW = average syllables per word
5913      var score = 206.835 - (1.015 * avgWordsPerSentence) - (84.6 * avgSyllablesPerWord);
5914
5915      // Clamp to 0-100 range
5916      return Math.max(0.0, Math.min(100.0, score));
5917   }

5919   /**
5920    * Converts an arbitrary object to a readable string format suitable for debugging and testing.
5921    *
5922    * <p>This method provides intelligent formatting for various Java types, recursively processing
5923    * nested structures to create human-readable representations. It's extensively used throughout
5924    * the Juneau framework for test assertions and debugging output.</p>
5925    *
5926    * <h5 class='section'>Type-Specific Formatting:</h5>
5927    * <ul>
5928    *    <li><b>null:</b> Returns <js>null</js></li>
5929    *    <li><b>Optional:</b> Recursively formats the contained value (or <js>null</js> if empty)</li>
5930    *    <li><b>Collections:</b> Formats as <js>"[item1,item2,item3]"</js> with comma-separated elements</li>
5931    *    <li><b>Maps:</b> Formats as <js>"{key1=value1,key2=value2}"</js> with comma-separated entries</li>
5932    *    <li><b>Map.Entry:</b> Formats as <js>"key=value"</js></li>
5933    *    <li><b>Arrays:</b> Converts to list format <js>"[item1,item2,item3]"</js></li>
5934    *    <li><b>Iterables/Iterators/Enumerations:</b> Converts to list and formats recursively</li>
5935    *    <li><b>GregorianCalendar:</b> Formats as ISO instant timestamp</li>
5936    *    <li><b>Date:</b> Formats as ISO instant string (e.g., <js>"2023-12-25T10:30:00Z"</js>)</li>
5937    *    <li><b>InputStream:</b> Converts to hexadecimal representation</li>
5938    *    <li><b>Reader:</b> Reads content and returns as string</li>
5939    *    <li><b>File:</b> Reads file content and returns as string</li>
5940    *    <li><b>byte[]:</b> Converts to hexadecimal representation</li>
5941    *    <li><b>Enum:</b> Returns the enum name via {@link Enum#name()}</li>
5942    *    <li><b>All other types:</b> Uses {@link Object#toString()}</li>
5943    * </ul>
5944    *
5945    * <h5 class='section'>Examples:</h5>
5946    * <p class='bjava'>
5947    *    <jc>// Collections</jc>
5948    *    readable(List.of("a", "b", "c")) <jc>// Returns: "[a,b,c]"</jc>
5949    *    readable(Set.of(1, 2, 3)) <jc>// Returns: "[1,2,3]" (order may vary)</jc>
5950    *
5951    *    <jc>// Maps</jc>
5952    *    readable(Map.of("foo", "bar", "baz", 123)) <jc>// Returns: "{foo=bar,baz=123}"</jc>
5953    *
5954    *    <jc>// Arrays</jc>
5955    *    readable(ints(1, 2, 3)) <jc>// Returns: "[1,2,3]"</jc>
5956    *    readable(new String[]{"a", "b"}) <jc>// Returns: "[a,b]"</jc>
5957    *
5958    *    <jc>// Nested structures</jc>
5959    *    readable(List.of(Map.of("x", 1), Set.of("a", "b"))) <jc>// Returns: "[{x=1},[a,b]]"</jc>
5960    *
5961    *    <jc>// Special types</jc>
5962    *    readable(Optional.of("test")) <jc>// Returns: "test"</jc>
5963    *    readable(Optional.empty()) <jc>// Returns: null</jc>
5964    *    readable(new Date(1640995200000L)) <jc>// Returns: "2022-01-01T00:00:00Z"</jc>
5965    *    readable(MyEnum.FOO) <jc>// Returns: "FOO"</jc>
5966    * </p>
5967    *
5968    * <h5 class='section'>Recursive Processing:</h5>
5969    * <p>The method recursively processes nested structures, so complex objects containing
5970    * collections, maps, and arrays are fully flattened into readable format. This makes it
5971    * ideal for test assertions where you need to compare complex object structures.</p>
5972    *
5973    * <h5 class='section'>Error Handling:</h5>
5974    * <p>IO operations (reading files, streams) are wrapped in safe() calls, converting
5975    * any exceptions to RuntimeExceptions. Binary data (InputStreams, byte arrays) is
5976    * converted to hexadecimal representation for readability.</p>
5977    *
5978    * @param o The object to convert to readable format. Can be <jk>null</jk>.
5979    * @return A readable string representation of the object, or <jk>null</jk> if the input was <jk>null</jk>.
5980    */
5981   public static String readable(Object o) {
5982      if (o == null)
5983         return null;
5984      var c = o.getClass();
5985
5986      // Special case for byte[] - must be handled before general array check
5987      if (c == byte[].class) {
5988         return toHex((byte[])o);
5989      }
5990
5991      // Check cache first
5992      var f = READIFIER_CACHE.get(c, () -> {
5993         // Find readifier from READIFIERS list
5994         // First try exact match, then isAssignableFrom
5995         var readifier = READIFIERS.stream()
5996            .filter(r -> r.forClass() == c || r.forClass().isAssignableFrom(c))
5997            .map(Readifier::toFunction)
5998            .findFirst()
5999            .orElse(null);
6000
6001         // If readifier found, use it
6002         if (readifier != null)
6003            return readifier;
6004
6005         // If no readifier found, check if it's an array
6006         if (c.isArray()) {
6007            return x -> {
6008               var l = list();
6009               for (var i = 0; i < Array.getLength(x); i++) {
6010                  l.add(Array.get(x, i));
6011               }
6012               return readable(l);
6013            };
6014         }
6015
6016         // If no readifier found, use toString() as fallback
6017         return Object::toString;
6018      });
6019
6020      return f.apply(o);
6021   }

6036    * @return The string with all occurrences of the substring removed, or <jk>null</jk> if input is <jk>null</jk>.
6037    */
6038   public static String remove(String str, String remove) {

6044   /**
6045    * Removes diacritical marks (accents) from characters in a string.
6046    *
6047    * <p>
6048    * Normalizes the string to NFD form and removes combining diacritical marks.
6049    *
6050    * <h5 class='section'>Example:</h5>
6051    * <p class='bjava'>
6052    *    removeAccents(<js>"café"</js>);     <jc>// "cafe"</jc>
6053    *    removeAccents(<js>"naïve"</js>);    <jc>// "naive"</jc>
6054    *    removeAccents(<js>"résumé"</js>);   <jc>// "resume"</jc>
6055    * </p>
6056    *
6057    * @param str The string to remove accents from. Can be <jk>null</jk>.
6058    * @return The string with accents removed, or <jk>null</jk> if input is <jk>null</jk>.
6059    */
6060   public static String removeAccents(String str) {
6061      if (str == null)
6062         return null;
6063
6064      // Normalize to NFD (decomposed form)
6065      var normalized = Normalizer.normalize(str, Normalizer.Form.NFD);
6066
6067      // Remove combining diacritical marks (Unicode category Mn)
6068      var sb = new StringBuilder(normalized.length());
6069      for (var i = 0; i < normalized.length(); i++) {
6070         var c = normalized.charAt(i);
6071         var type = Character.getType(c);
6072         // Mn = Nonspacing_Mark (combining marks)
6073         if (type != Character.NON_SPACING_MARK) {
6074            sb.append(c);
6075         }
6076      }
6077
6078      return sb.toString();
6079   }

6082    * Removes multiple substrings from a string.

6086    *    removeAll(<js>"hello world test"</js>, <js>"hello"</js>, <js>"test"</js>);  <jc>// " world "</jc>
6087    *    removeAll(<jk>null</jk>, <js>"x"</js>);                                     <jc>// null</jc>
6088    * </p>
6089    *
6090    * @param str The string to process.
6091    * @param remove The substrings to remove.
6092    * @return The string with all specified substrings removed, or <jk>null</jk> if input is <jk>null</jk>.
6093    */
6094   public static String removeAll(String str, String...remove) {
6095      if (str == null)
6096         return null;
6097      if (isEmpty(str) || remove == null || remove.length == 0)
6098         return str;
6099      var result = str;
6100      for (var r : remove) {
6101         if (r != null)
6102            result = result.replace(r, "");
6103      }
6104      return result;
6105   }

6107   /**
6108    * Removes control characters from a string, replacing them with spaces.
6109    *
6110    * <h5 class='section'>Example:</h5>
6111    * <p class='bjava'>
6112    *    removeControlChars(<js>"hello\u0000\u0001world"</js>);   <jc>// "hello  world"</jc>
6113    *    removeControlChars(<js>"hello\nworld"</js>);             <jc>// "hello\nworld"</jc>
6114    * </p>
6115    *
6116    * @param str The string to process.
6117    * @return The string with control characters replaced by spaces (except whitespace control chars), or <jk>null</jk> if input is <jk>null</jk>.
6118    */
6119   public static String removeControlChars(String str) {
6120      if (str == null)
6121         return null;
6122      var sb = new StringBuilder();
6123      for (var i = 0; i < str.length(); i++) {
6124         var c = str.charAt(i);
6125         if (Character.isISOControl(c) && ! Character.isWhitespace(c))
6126            sb.append(' ');
6127         else
6128            sb.append(c);
6129      }
6130      return sb.toString();
6131   }

6196   /**

6200    * This method is commonly used to process numeric literals that may contain underscores for readability
6201    * (e.g., <js>"1_000_000"</js> becomes <js>"1000000"</js>), as Java allows underscores in numeric literals
6202    * but some parsing methods do not support them.
6203    *
6204    * <p>
6205    * If the string does not contain any underscores, the original string is returned (no new object created).
6206    *
6207    * <h5 class='section'>Example:</h5>
6208    * <p class='bjava'>
6209    *    removeUnderscores(<js>"1_000_000"</js>);        <jc>// "1000000"</jc>
6210    *    removeUnderscores(<js>"1_000.5"</js>);          <jc>// "1000.5"</jc>
6211    *    removeUnderscores(<js>"hello_world"</js>);      <jc>// "helloworld"</jc>
6212    *    removeUnderscores(<js>"no_underscores"</js>);   <jc>// "nounderscores"</jc>
6213    *    removeUnderscores(<js>"Hello"</js>);            <jc>// "Hello" (no change, same object returned)</jc>
6214    * </p>
6215    *
6216    * @param value The string from which to remove underscores. Must not be <jk>null</jk>.
6217    * @return A new string with all underscores removed, or the original string if it contains no underscores.
6218    * @throws IllegalArgumentException If <c>value</c> is <jk>null</jk>.
6219    * @see #parseInt(String)
6220    * @see #parseLong(String)
6221    * @see #parseFloat(String)
6222    * @see #parseNumber(String, Class)
6223    */
6224   public static String removeUnderscores(String value) {
6225      reqnn("value", value);
6226      return notContains(value, '_') ? value : value.replace("_", "");
6227   }

6229   /**
6230    * Creates a repeated pattern.
6231    *
6232    * @param count The number of times to repeat the pattern.
6233    * @param pattern The pattern to repeat.  Must not be <jk>null</jk> (a <jk>null</jk> argument throws {@link NullPointerException}).
6234    * @return A new string consisting of the repeated pattern.
6235    */
6236   public static String repeat(int count, String pattern) {
6237      var sb = new StringBuilder(pattern.length() * count);
6238      for (var i = 0; i < count; i++)
6239         sb.append(pattern);
6240      return sb.toString();
6241   }

6243   /**
6244    * Replaces <js>"\\uXXXX"</js> character sequences with their unicode characters.
6245    *
6246    * @param s The string to replace unicode sequences in.  Must not be <jk>null</jk> (a <jk>null</jk> argument throws {@link NullPointerException}).
6247    * @return A string with unicode sequences replaced.
6248    */
6249   public static String replaceUnicodeSequences(String s) {
6250
6251      if (s.indexOf('\\') == -1)
6252         return s;
6253
6254      var p = Pattern.compile("\\\\u(\\p{XDigit}{4})");
6255      var m = p.matcher(s);
6256      var sb = new StringBuffer(s.length());
6257
6258      while (m.find()) {
6259         var ch = String.valueOf((char)Integer.parseInt(m.group(1), 16));
6260         m.appendReplacement(sb, Matcher.quoteReplacement(ch));
6261      }
6262
6263      m.appendTail(sb);
6264      return sb.toString();
6265   }

6291    *    right(<jk>null</jk>, 3);          <jc>// null</jc>
6292    *    right(<js>""</js>, 3);            <jc>// ""</jc>
6293    *    right(<js>"hello"</js>, 3);       <jc>// "llo"</jc>

6295    * </p>
6296    *
6297    * @param str The string to get characters from.
6298    * @param len The number of characters to get.
6299    * @return The rightmost characters, or <jk>null</jk> if input is <jk>null</jk>.
6300    */
6301   public static String right(String str, int len) {
6302      if (str == null)
6303         return null;
6304      if (len < 0)
6305         return "";
6306      if (len >= str.length())
6307         return str;
6308      return str.substring(str.length() - len);
6309   }

6321    *    sanitize(<js>"Hello &lt;b&gt;World&lt;/b&gt;"</js>);                <jc>// "Hello &amp;lt;b&amp;gt;World&amp;lt;/b&amp;gt;"</jc>
6322    * </p>

6325    * @return The sanitized string with HTML/XML tags escaped, or <jk>null</jk> if input is <jk>null</jk>.

6334   /**
6335    * Calculates the similarity percentage between two strings using Levenshtein distance.
6336    *
6337    * <p>
6338    * Returns a value between 0.0 (completely different) and 1.0 (identical).
6339    *
6340    * <h5 class='section'>Example:</h5>
6341    * <p class='bjava'>
6342    *    similarity(<js>"hello"</js>, <js>"hello"</js>);           <jc>// 1.0 (100%)</jc>
6343    *    similarity(<js>"kitten"</js>, <js>"sitting"</js>);        <jc>// ~0.57 (57%)</jc>
6344    *    similarity(<js>"abc"</js>, <js>"xyz"</js>);               <jc>// 0.0 (0%)</jc>
6345    * </p>
6346    *
6347    * @param str1 The first string.  Can be <jk>null</jk> (treated as empty).
6348    * @param str2 The second string.  Can be <jk>null</jk> (treated as empty).
6349    * @return A similarity value between 0.0 and 1.0, where 1.0 means identical.
6350    */
6351   public static double similarity(String str1, String str2) {
6352      if (str1 == null)
6353         str1 = "";
6354      if (str2 == null)
6355         str2 = "";
6356
6357      if (str1.equals(str2))
6358         return 1.0;
6359
6360      var maxLen = Math.max(str1.length(), str2.length());
6361
6362      var distance = levenshteinDistance(str1, str2);
6363      return 1.0 - ((double)distance / maxLen);
6364   }

6366   /**
6367    * Converts a string to snake_case format.
6368    *
6369    * <p>
6370    * Handles various input formats:
6371    * <ul>
6372    *   <li>Space-separated: "hello world" → "hello_world"</li>
6373    *   <li>CamelCase: "helloWorld" → "hello_world"</li>
6374    *   <li>PascalCase: "HelloWorld" → "hello_world"</li>
6375    *   <li>Kebab-case: "hello-world" → "hello_world"</li>
6376    * </ul>
6377    *
6378    * <h5 class='section'>Example:</h5>
6379    * <p class='bjava'>
6380    *    snakeCase(<jk>null</jk>);                    <jc>// null</jc>
6381    *    snakeCase(<js>""</js>);                      <jc>// ""</jc>
6382    *    snakeCase(<js>"hello world"</js>);           <jc>// "hello_world"</jc>
6383    *    snakeCase(<js>"helloWorld"</js>);            <jc>// "hello_world"</jc>
6384    *    snakeCase(<js>"HelloWorld"</js>);            <jc>// "hello_world"</jc>
6385    *    snakeCase(<js>"hello-world"</js>);           <jc>// "hello_world"</jc>
6386    * </p>
6387    *
6388    * @param str The string to convert.
6389    * @return The snake_case string, or <jk>null</jk> if input is <jk>null</jk>.
6390    */
6391   public static String snakeCase(String str) {
6392      if (str == null)
6393         return null;
6394      if (isEmpty(str))
6395         return str;
6396
6397      var words = splitWords(str);
6398      if (words.isEmpty())
6399         return "";
6400
6401      var result = new StringBuilder();
6402      for (var i = 0; i < words.size(); i++) {
6403         if (i > 0)
6404            result.append('_');
6405         result.append(lowerCaseRoot(words.get(i)));
6406      }
6407
6408      return result.toString();
6409   }

6411   /**
6412    * Sorts a string array in natural order.
6413    *
6414    * <p>
6415    * Returns <jk>null</jk> if the array is <jk>null</jk>.
6416    * This method creates a copy of the array and sorts it, leaving the original array unchanged.
6417    *
6418    * <h5 class='section'>Examples:</h5>
6419    * <p class='bjava'>
6420    *    String[] <jv>array</jv> = {<js>"zebra"</js>, <js>"apple"</js>, <js>"banana"</js>};
6421    *    String[] <jv>sorted</jv> = sort(<jv>array</jv>);
6422    *    <jc>// Returns: ["apple", "banana", "zebra"]</jc>
6423    * </p>
6424    *
6425    * @param array The array to sort. Can be <jk>null</jk>.
6426    * @return A new sorted array, or an empty array if the array was <jk>null</jk>.
6427    */
6428   public static String[] sort(String[] array) {
6429      if (array == null)
6430         return new String[0];
6431      var result = Arrays.copyOf(array, array.length);
6432      Arrays.sort(result);
6433      return result;
6434   }

6436   /**
6437    * Sorts a string array in case-insensitive order.
6438    *
6439    * <p>
6440    * Returns <jk>null</jk> if the array is <jk>null</jk>.
6441    * This method creates a copy of the array and sorts it using case-insensitive comparison,
6442    * leaving the original array unchanged.
6443    *
6444    * <h5 class='section'>Examples:</h5>
6445    * <p class='bjava'>
6446    *    String[] <jv>array</jv> = {<js>"Zebra"</js>, <js>"apple"</js>, <js>"Banana"</js>};
6447    *    String[] <jv>sorted</jv> = sortIgnoreCase(<jv>array</jv>);
6448    *    <jc>// Returns: ["apple", "Banana", "Zebra"]</jc>
6449    * </p>
6450    *
6451    * @param array The array to sort. Can be <jk>null</jk>.
6452    * @return A new sorted array (case-insensitive), or an empty array if the array was <jk>null</jk>.
6453    */
6454   public static String[] sortIgnoreCase(String[] array) {
6455      if (array == null)
6456         return new String[0];
6457      var result = Arrays.copyOf(array, array.length);
6458      Arrays.sort(result, String.CASE_INSENSITIVE_ORDER);
6459      return result;
6460   }

6462   /**
6463    * Generates a Soundex code for a string.
6464    *
6465    * <p>
6466    * Soundex is a phonetic algorithm for indexing names by sound. The code consists of
6467    * a letter followed by three digits. Similar-sounding names produce the same code.
6468    *
6469    * <h5 class='section'>Example:</h5>
6470    * <p class='bjava'>
6471    *    soundex(<js>"Smith"</js>);   <jc>// "S530"</jc>
6472    *    soundex(<js>"Smythe"</js>);  <jc>// "S530"</jc>
6473    *    soundex(<js>"Robert"</js>);  <jc>// "R163"</jc>
6474    * </p>
6475    *
6476    * @param str The string to generate a Soundex code for. Can be <jk>null</jk>.
6477    * @return The Soundex code (1 letter + 3 digits), or <jk>null</jk> if input is <jk>null</jk> or empty.
6478    */
6479   public static String soundex(String str) {
6480      if (isEmpty(str))
6481         return null;
6482
6483      var upper = str.toUpperCase(Locale.ROOT);
6484      var result = new StringBuilder(4);
6485      result.append(upper.charAt(0));
6486
6487      // Soundex mapping: 0 = AEIOUHWY, 1 = BFPV, 2 = CGJKQSXZ, 3 = DT, 4 = L, 5 = MN, 6 = R
6488      // H/W/Y don't get codes but don't break sequences either
6489      // Initialize lastCode to a value that won't match any real code
6490      var lastCode = '\0';
6491
6492      for (var i = 1; i < upper.length() && result.length() < 4; i++) {
6493         var c = upper.charAt(i);
6494         var code = getSoundexCode(c);
6495         if (code == '0') {
6496            // H/W/Y/vowels - don't add code, but don't update lastCode either
6497            // This allows sequences to continue across H/W/Y/vowels
6498            continue;
6499         }
6500         if (code != lastCode) {
6501            result.append(code);
6502            lastCode = code;
6503         }
6504         // If code == lastCode, skip it (consecutive same codes)
6505      }
6506
6507      // Pad with zeros if needed
6508      while (result.length() < 4) {
6509         result.append('0');
6510      }
6511
6512      return result.toString();
6513   }

6525   /**
6526    * Splits a character-delimited string into a string array.
6527    *
6528    * <p>
6529    * Does not split on escaped-delimiters (e.g. "\,");
6530    * Resulting tokens are trimmed of whitespace.
6531    *
6532    * <p>
6533    * <b>NOTE:</b>  This behavior is different than the Jakarta equivalent.
6534    * split("a,b,c",',') -&gt; {"a","b","c"}
6535    * split("a, b ,c ",',') -&gt; {"a","b","c"}
6536    * split("a,,c",',') -&gt; {"a","","c"}
6537    * split(",,",',') -&gt; {"","",""}
6538    * split("",',') -&gt; {}
6539    * split(null,',') -&gt; {}
6540    * split("a,b\,c,d", ',', false) -&gt; {"a","b\,c","d"}
6541    * split("a,b\\,c,d", ',', false) -&gt; {"a","b\","c","d"}
6542    * split("a,b\,c,d", ',', true) -&gt; {"a","b,c","d"}
6543    *
6544    * @param s The string to split.  Can be <jk>null</jk>.
6545    * @param c The character to split on.
6546    * @return The tokens, or an empty list if the string was <jk>null</jk>.
6547    */
6548   public static List<String> split(String s, char c) {
6549      return split(s, c, Integer.MAX_VALUE);
6550   }

6552   /**
6553    * Same as {@link #splita(String, char)} but consumes the tokens instead of creating an array.
6554    *
6555    * @param s The string to split.  Can be <jk>null</jk> (no tokens are consumed).
6556    * @param c The character to split on.
6557    * @param consumer The consumer of the tokens.  Must not be <jk>null</jk> when the string is non-empty.
6558    */
6559   public static void split(String s, char c, Consumer<String> consumer) {
6560      var escapeChars = getEscapeSet(c);
6561
6562      if (isEmpty(s))
6563         return;
6564      if (s.indexOf(c) == -1) {
6565         consumer.accept(s);
6566         return;
6567      }
6568
6569      var x1 = 0;
6570      var escapeCount = 0;
6571
6572      for (var i = 0; i < s.length(); i++) {
6573         if (s.charAt(i) == '\\')
6574            escapeCount++;
6575         else if (s.charAt(i) == c && escapeCount % 2 == 0) {
6576            var s2 = s.substring(x1, i);
6577            var s3 = unescapeChars(s2, escapeChars);
6578            consumer.accept(s3.trim());
6579            x1 = i + 1;
6580         }
6581         if (s.charAt(i) != '\\')
6582            escapeCount = 0;
6583      }
6584      var s2 = s.substring(x1);
6585      var s3 = unescapeChars(s2, escapeChars);
6586      consumer.accept(s3.trim());
6587   }

6589   /**
6590    * Same as {@link #splita(String, char, int)} but returns a {@link List}.
6591    *
6592    * @param s The string to split.  Can be <jk>null</jk>.
6593    * @param c The character to split on.
6594    * @param limit The maximum number of tokens to return.
6595    * @return The tokens, or an empty list if the string was <jk>null</jk>.
6596    */
6597   public static List<String> split(String s, char c, int limit) {
6598
6599      var escapeChars = getEscapeSet(c);
6600
6601      if (s == null)
6602         return Collections.emptyList();
6603      if (isEmpty(s))
6604         return Collections.emptyList();
6605      if (s.indexOf(c) == -1)
6606         return Collections.singletonList(s);
6607
6608      var l = new LinkedList<String>();
6609      var sArray = s.toCharArray();
6610      var x1 = 0;
6611      var escapeCount = 0;
6612      limit--;
6613      for (var i = 0; i < sArray.length && limit > 0; i++) {
6614         if (sArray[i] == '\\')
6615            escapeCount++;
6616         else if (sArray[i] == c && escapeCount % 2 == 0) {
6617            var s2 = new String(sArray, x1, i - x1);
6618            var s3 = unescapeChars(s2, escapeChars);
6619            l.add(s3.trim());
6620            limit--;
6621            x1 = i + 1;
6622         }
6623         if (sArray[i] != '\\')
6624            escapeCount = 0;
6625      }
6626      var s2 = new String(sArray, x1, sArray.length - x1);
6627      var s3 = unescapeChars(s2, escapeChars);
6628      l.add(s3.trim());
6629
6630      return l;
6631   }

6669    * split("a,b\\,c,d", ',', false) -&gt; {"a","b\","c","d"}

6715   /**
6716    * Splits a list of key-value pairs into an ordered map.
6717    *
6718    * <p>
6719    * Example:
6720    * <p class='bjava'>
6721    *    String <jv>in</jv> = <js>"foo=1;bar=2"</js>;
6722    *    Map <jv>map</jv> = StringUtils.<jsm>splitMap</jsm>(in, <js>';'</js>, <js>'='</js>, <jk>true</jk>);
6723    * </p>
6724    *
6725    * @param s The string to split.
6726    * @param trim Trim strings after parsing.
6727    * @return The parsed map, or an empty map if the string was null.
6728    */
6729   public static Map<String,String> splitMap(String s, boolean trim) {
6730
6731      if (s == null)
6732         return emptyMap();
6733      if (isEmpty(s))
6734         return emptyMap();
6735
6736      var m = new LinkedHashMap<String,String>();
6737
6738      // S1: Found start of key, looking for equals.
6739      // S2: Found equals, looking for delimiter (or end).
6740
6741      var state = S1;
6742
6743      var sArray = s.toCharArray();
6744      var x1 = 0;
6745      var escapeCount = 0;
6746      String key = null;
6747      for (var i = 0; i < sArray.length + 1; i++) {
6748         var c = i == sArray.length ? ',' : sArray[i];
6749         if (c == '\\')
6750            escapeCount++;
6751         if (escapeCount % 2 == 0) {
6752            if (state == S1) {
6753               if (c == '=') {
6754                  key = s.substring(x1, i);
6755                  if (trim)
6756                     key = trim(key);
6757                  key = unescapeChars(key, MAP_ESCAPE_SET);
6758                  state = S2;
6759                  x1 = i + 1;
6760               } else if (c == ',') {
6761                  key = s.substring(x1, i);
6762                  if (trim)
6763                     key = trim(key);
6764                  key = unescapeChars(key, MAP_ESCAPE_SET);
6765                  m.put(key, "");
6766                  state = S1;
6767                  x1 = i + 1;
6768               }
6769            } else /* state == S2 */ {
6770               if (c == ',') {
6771                  var val = s.substring(x1, i);
6772                  if (trim)
6773                     val = trim(val);
6774                  val = unescapeChars(val, MAP_ESCAPE_SET);
6775                  m.put(key, val);
6776                  key = null;
6777                  x1 = i + 1;
6778                  state = S1;
6779               }
6780            }
6781         }
6782         if (c != '\\')
6783            escapeCount = 0;
6784      }
6785
6786      return m;
6787   }

6789   /**
6790    * Splits the method arguments in the signature of a method.
6791    *
6792    * @param s The arguments to split.  Can be <jk>null</jk> (returns an empty array).
6793    * @return The split arguments, or an empty array if the input string is <jk>null</jk> or empty.
6794    */
6795   public static String[] splitMethodArgs(String s) {
6796
6797      if (s == null)
6798         return new String[0];
6799      if (isEmpty(s))
6800         return new String[0];
6801      if (s.indexOf(',') == -1)
6802         return array(s);
6803
6804      var l = new LinkedList<String>();
6805      var sArray = s.toCharArray();
6806      var x1 = 0;
6807      var paramDepth = 0;
6808
6809      for (var i = 0; i < sArray.length; i++) {
6810         var c = s.charAt(i);
6811         if (c == '>')
6812            paramDepth++;
6813         else if (c == '<')
6814            paramDepth--;
6815         else if (c == ',' && paramDepth == 0) {
6816            var s2 = new String(sArray, x1, i - x1);
6817            l.add(s2.trim());
6818            x1 = i + 1;
6819         }
6820      }
6821
6822      var s2 = new String(sArray, x1, sArray.length - x1);
6823      l.add(s2.trim());
6824
6825      return l.toArray(new String[l.size()]);
6826   }

6828   /**
6829    * Splits a comma-delimited list containing "nesting constructs".
6830    *
6831    * Nesting constructs are simple embedded "{...}" comma-delimted lists.
6832    *
6833    * Example:
6834    *    "a{b,c},d" -> ["a{b,c}","d"]
6835    *
6836    * Handles escapes and trims whitespace from tokens.
6837    *
6838    * @param s The input string.
6839    * @return
6840    *    The results, or an empty list if the input was <jk>null</jk>.
6841    *    <br>An empty string results in an empty list.
6842    */
6843   public static List<String> splitNested(String s) {
6844      var escapeChars = getEscapeSet(',');
6845
6846      if (s == null)
6847         return Collections.emptyList();
6848      if (isEmpty(s))
6849         return Collections.emptyList();
6850      if (s.indexOf(',') == -1)
6851         return Collections.singletonList(trim(s));
6852
6853      var l = new LinkedList<String>();
6854
6855      var x1 = 0;
6856      var inEscape = false;
6857      var depthCount = 0;
6858
6859      for (var i = 0; i < s.length(); i++) {
6860         var c = s.charAt(i);
6861         if (inEscape) {
6862            if (c == '\\') {
6863               inEscape = false;
6864            }
6865         } else {
6866            if (c == '\\') {
6867               inEscape = true;
6868            } else if (c == '{') {
6869               depthCount++;
6870            } else if (c == '}') {
6871               depthCount--;
6872            } else if (c == ',' && depthCount == 0) {
6873               l.add(trim(unescapeChars(s.substring(x1, i), escapeChars)));
6874               x1 = i + 1;
6875            }
6876         }
6877      }
6878      l.add(trim(unescapeChars(s.substring(x1, s.length()), escapeChars)));
6879
6880      return l;
6881   }
6882
6883   /**
6884    * Splits a nested comma-delimited list.
6885    *
6886    * Nesting constructs are simple embedded "{...}" comma-delimted lists.
6887    *
6888    * Example:
6889    *    "a{b,c{d,e}}" -> ["b","c{d,e}"]
6890    *
6891    * Handles escapes and trims whitespace from tokens.
6892    *
6893    * @param s The input string.  Must not be <jk>null</jk> or empty (a <jk>null</jk> or empty argument throws {@link IllegalArgumentException}).
6894    * @return
6895    *    The results.
6896    * @throws IllegalArgumentException If the input was <jk>null</jk> or empty.
6897    */
6898   public static List<String> splitNestedInner(String s) {
6899      req(isNotNull(s), "String was null.");
6900      req(isNotEmpty(s), "String was empty.");
6901
6902      // S1: Looking for '{'
6903      // S2: Found '{', looking for '}'
6904
6905      var start = -1;
6906      var end = -1;
6907      var state = S1;
6908
6909      var depth = 0;
6910      var inEscape = false;
6911
6912      for (var i = 0; i < s.length(); i++) {
6913         var c = s.charAt(i);
6914         if (inEscape) {
6915            if (c == '\\') {
6916               inEscape = false;
6917            }
6918         } else {
6919            if (c == '\\') {
6920               inEscape = true;
6921            } else if (state == S1) {
6922               if (c == '{') {
6923                  start = i + 1;
6924                  state = S2;
6925               }
6926            } else /* state == S2 */ {
6927               if (c == '{') {
6928                  depth++;
6929               } else if (depth > 0 && c == '}') {
6930                  depth--;
6931               } else if (c == '}') {
6932                  end = i;
6933                  break;
6934               }
6935            }
6936         }
6937      }
6938
6939      if (start == -1)
6940         throw iaex("Start character { not found in string:  %s", s);
6941      if (end == -1)
6942         throw iaex("End character } not found in string  %s", s);
6943      return splitNested(s.substring(start, end));
6944   }
6945
6946   /**
6947    * Splits a space-delimited string with optionally quoted arguments.
6948    *
6949    * <p>
6950    * Examples:
6951    * <ul>
6952    *    <li><js>"foo"</js> =&gt; <c>["foo"]</c>
6953    *    <li><js>" foo "</js> =&gt; <c>["foo"]</c>
6954    *    <li><js>"foo bar baz"</js> =&gt; <c>["foo","bar","baz"]</c>
6955    *    <li><js>"foo 'bar baz'"</js> =&gt; <c>["foo","bar baz"]</c>
6956    *    <li><js>"foo \"bar baz\""</js> =&gt; <c>["foo","bar baz"]</c>
6957    *    <li><js>"foo 'bar\'baz'"</js> =&gt; <c>["foo","bar'baz"]</c>
6958    * </ul>
6959    *
6960    * @param s The input string.  Can be <jk>null</jk> (returns an empty array).
6961    * @return
6962    *    The results, or an empty array if the input was <jk>null</jk>.
6963    *    <br>An empty string results in an empty array.
6964    */
6965   public static String[] splitQuoted(String s) {
6966      return splitQuoted(s, false);
6967   }

6969   /**
6970    * Same as {@link StringUtils#splitQuoted(String)} but allows you to optionally keep the quote characters.
6971    *
6972    * @param s The input string.  Can be <jk>null</jk> (returns an empty array).
6973    * @param keepQuotes If <jk>true</jk>, quote characters are kept on the tokens.
6974    * @return
6975    *    The results, or an empty array if the input was <jk>null</jk>.
6976    *    <br>An empty string results in an empty array.
6977    */
6978   @SuppressWarnings({
6979      "java:S2583" // State variables persist across loop iterations
6980   })
6981   public static String[] splitQuoted(String s, boolean keepQuotes) {
6982
6983      if (s == null)
6984         return new String[0];
6985
6986      s = s.trim();
6987
6988      if (isEmpty(s))
6989         return array();
6990
6991      if (! containsAny(s, ' ', '\t', '\'', '"'))
6992         return array(s);
6993
6994      // S1: Looking for start of token.
6995      // S2: Found ', looking for end '
6996      // S3: Found ", looking for end "
6997      // S4: Found non-whitespace, looking for end whitespace.
6998
6999      var state = S1;
7000
7001      var isInEscape = false;
7002      var needsUnescape = false;
7003      var mark = 0;
7004
7005      var l = new ArrayList<String>();
7006      for (var i = 0; i < s.length(); i++) {
7007         var c = s.charAt(i);
7008
7009         if (state == S1) {
7010            if (c == '\'') {
7011               state = S2;
7012               mark = keepQuotes ? i : i + 1;
7013            } else if (c == '"') {
7014               state = S3;
7015               mark = keepQuotes ? i : i + 1;
7016            } else if (c != ' ' && c != '\t') {
7017               state = S4;
7018               mark = i;
7019            }
7020         } else if (state == S2 || state == S3) {
7021            if (c == '\\') {
7022               isInEscape = ! isInEscape;
7023               if (isInEscape)
7024                  needsUnescape = ! keepQuotes;
7025            } else if (! isInEscape) {
7026               if (c == (state == S2 ? '\'' : '"')) {
7027                  var s2 = s.substring(mark, keepQuotes ? i + 1 : i);
7028                  if (needsUnescape)
7029                     s2 = unescapeChars(s2, QUOTE_ESCAPE_SET);
7030                  l.add(s2);
7031                  state = S1;
7032                  isInEscape = needsUnescape = false;
7033               }
7034            } else {
7035               isInEscape = false;
7036            }
7037         } else /* state == S4 */ {
7038            if (c == ' ' || c == '\t') {
7039               l.add(s.substring(mark, i));
7040               state = S1;
7041            }
7042         }
7043      }
7044      if (state == S4)
7045         l.add(s.substring(mark));
7046      else if (state == S2 || state == S3)
7047         throw iaex("Unmatched string quotes: %s", s);
7048      return l.toArray(new String[l.size()]);
7049   }

7051   /**
7052    * An efficient method for checking if a string starts with a character.
7053    *
7054    * @param s The string to check.  Can be <jk>null</jk>.
7055    * @param c The character to check for.
7056    * @return <jk>true</jk> if the specified string is not <jk>null</jk> and starts with the specified character.
7057    */
7058   public static boolean startsWith(String s, char c) {
7059      if (isNotNull(s)) {
7060         var i = s.length();
7061         if (i > 0)
7062            return s.charAt(0) == c;
7063      }
7064      return false;
7065   }

7111   /**
7112    * Strips invalid characters such as CTRL characters from a string meant to be encoded
7113    * as an HTTP header value.
7114    *
7115    * @param s The string to strip chars from.
7116    * @return The string with invalid characters removed.
7117    */
7118   public static String stripInvalidHttpHeaderChars(String s) {
7119
7120      if (s == null)
7121         return null;
7122
7123      var needsReplace = false;
7124      for (var i = 0; i < s.length() && ! needsReplace; i++)
7125         needsReplace |= HTTP_HEADER_CHARS.contains(s.charAt(i));
7126
7127      if (! needsReplace)
7128         return s;
7129
7130      var sb = new StringBuilder(s.length());
7131      for (var i = 0; i < s.length(); i++) {
7132         var c = s.charAt(i);
7133         if (HTTP_HEADER_CHARS.contains(c))
7134            sb.append(c);
7135      }
7136
7137      return sb.toString();

7140   /**

7142    *
7143    * <h5 class='section'>Example:</h5>
7144    * <p class='bjava'>
7145    *    substringAfter(<jk>null</jk>, <js>"."</js>);              <jc>// null</jc>
7146    *    substringAfter(<js>"hello.world"</js>, <jk>null</jk>);    <jc>// ""</jc>
7147    *    substringAfter(<js>"hello.world"</js>, <js>"."</js>);     <jc>// "world"</jc>
7148    *    substringAfter(<js>"hello.world"</js>, <js>"xyz"</js>);   <jc>// ""</jc>
7149    * </p>

7151    * @param str The string to get a substring from.
7152    * @param separator The separator string.
7153    * @return The substring after the first occurrence of the separator, or empty string if separator not found.
7154    */
7155   public static String substringAfter(String str, String separator) {
7156      if (isEmpty(str))
7157         return str;
7158      if (separator == null)
7159         return "";
7160      var pos = str.indexOf(separator);

7163      return str.substring(pos + separator.length());

7173    *    substringBefore(<js>"hello.world"</js>, <js>"."</js>);     <jc>// "hello"</jc>

7190   /**
7191    * Returns the substring between two delimiters.
7192    *
7193    * <h5 class='section'>Example:</h5>
7194    * <p class='bjava'>
7195    *    substringBetween(<jk>null</jk>, <js>"&lt;"</js>, <js>"&gt;"</js>);              <jc>// null</jc>
7196    *    substringBetween(<js>"&lt;hello&gt;"</js>, <js>"&lt;"</js>, <js>"&gt;"</js>);   <jc>// "hello"</jc>
7197    *    substringBetween(<js>"&lt;hello&gt;"</js>, <js>"["</js>, <js>"]"</js>);         <jc>// null</jc>
7198    * </p>
7199    *
7200    * @param str The string to get a substring from.
7201    * @param open The opening delimiter.
7202    * @param close The closing delimiter.
7203    * @return The substring between the delimiters, or <jk>null</jk> if delimiters not found.
7204    */
7205   public static String substringBetween(String str, String open, String close) {
7206      if (str == null || open == null || close == null)
7207         return null;
7208      var start = str.indexOf(open);
7209      if (start == -1)
7210         return null;
7211      var end = str.indexOf(close, start + open.length());
7212      if (end == -1)
7213         return null;
7214      return str.substring(start + open.length(), end);
7215   }

7217   /**
7218    * Swaps the case of all characters in a string.
7219    *
7220    * <h5 class='section'>Example:</h5>
7221    * <p class='bjava'>
7222    *    swapCase(<js>"Hello World"</js>);   <jc>// "hELLO wORLD"</jc>
7223    *    swapCase(<js>"ABC123xyz"</js>);     <jc>// "abc123XYZ"</jc>
7224    * </p>
7225    *
7226    * @param str The string to process.
7227    * @return The string with case swapped, or <jk>null</jk> if input is <jk>null</jk>.
7228    */
7229   public static String swapCase(String str) {
7230      if (str == null)
7231         return null;
7232      var sb = new StringBuilder(str.length());
7233      for (var i = 0; i < str.length(); i++) {
7234         var c = str.charAt(i);
7235         if (LETTER_UC.contains(c))
7236            sb.append(Character.toLowerCase(c));
7237         else if (LETTER_LC.contains(c))
7238            sb.append(Character.toUpperCase(c));
7239         else
7240            sb.append(c);
7241      }
7242      return sb.toString();
7243   }

7245   /**
7246    * Converts a string to Title Case format (first letter of each word capitalized, separated by spaces).
7247    *
7248    * <p>
7249    * Handles various input formats:
7250    * <ul>
7251    *   <li>CamelCase: "helloWorld" → "Hello World"</li>
7252    *   <li>PascalCase: "HelloWorld" → "Hello World"</li>
7253    *   <li>Snake_case: "hello_world" → "Hello World"</li>
7254    *   <li>Kebab-case: "hello-world" → "Hello World"</li>
7255    * </ul>
7256    *
7257    * <h5 class='section'>Example:</h5>
7258    * <p class='bjava'>
7259    *    titleCase(<jk>null</jk>);                    <jc>// null</jc>
7260    *    titleCase(<js>""</js>);                      <jc>// ""</jc>
7261    *    titleCase(<js>"hello world"</js>);           <jc>// "Hello World"</jc>
7262    *    titleCase(<js>"helloWorld"</js>);            <jc>// "Hello World"</jc>
7263    *    titleCase(<js>"hello_world"</js>);           <jc>// "Hello World"</jc>
7264    *    titleCase(<js>"hello-world"</js>);           <jc>// "Hello World"</jc>
7265    * </p>
7266    *
7267    * @param str The string to convert.
7268    * @return The Title Case string, or <jk>null</jk> if input is <jk>null</jk>.
7269    */
7270   public static String titleCase(String str) {
7271      if (str == null)
7272         return null;
7273      if (isEmpty(str))
7274         return str;
7275
7276      var words = splitWords(str);
7277      if (words.isEmpty())
7278         return "";
7279
7280      var result = new StringBuilder();
7281      for (var i = 0; i < words.size(); i++) {
7282         if (i > 0)
7283            result.append(' ');
7284         result.append(capitalize(words.get(i).toLowerCase()));
7285      }
7286
7287      return result.toString();
7288   }

7290   /**
7291    * Converts the specified object to a comma-delimited list.
7292    *
7293    * @param o The object to convert.  Can be <jk>null</jk> (returns <jk>null</jk>).
7294    * @return The specified object as a comma-delimited list, or <jk>null</jk> if the input was <jk>null</jk>.
7295    */
7296   public static String toCdl(Object o) {
7297      if (o == null)
7298         return null;
7299      if (ClassUtils.isArray(o)) {
7300         var sb = new StringBuilder();
7301         for (int i = 0, j = Array.getLength(o); i < j; i++) {
7302            if (i > 0)
7303               sb.append(", ");
7304            sb.append(Array.get(o, i));
7305         }
7306         return sb.toString();
7307      }
7308      if (o instanceof Collection<?> o2)
7309         return join(o2, ", ");
7310      return o.toString();
7311   }

7313   /**
7314    * Converts the specified byte into a 2 hexadecimal characters.
7315    *
7316    * @param b The number to convert to hex.
7317    * @return A <code><jk>char</jk>[2]</code> containing the specified characters.
7318    */
7319   public static String toHex(byte b) {
7320      var c = new char[2];
7321      var v = b & 0xFF;
7322      c[0] = HEX[v >>> 4];
7323      c[1] = HEX[v & 0x0F];
7324      return new String(c);

7352   /**
7353    * Converts the specified number into a 2 hexadecimal characters.
7354    *
7355    * @param num The number to convert to hex.
7356    * @return A <code><jk>char</jk>[2]</code> containing the specified characters.
7357    */
7358   public static char[] toHex2(int num) {
7359      if (num < 0 || num > 255)
7360         throw new NumberFormatException("toHex2 can only be used on numbers between 0 and 255");
7361      var n = new char[2];
7362      var a = num % 16;
7363      n[1] = (char)(a > 9 ? 'A' + a - 10 : '0' + a);
7364      a = (num / 16) % 16;
7365      n[0] = (char)(a > 9 ? 'A' + a - 10 : '0' + a);
7366      return n;
7367   }

7369   /**
7370    * Converts the specified number into a 4 hexadecimal characters.
7371    *
7372    * @param num The number to convert to hex.
7373    * @return A <code><jk>char</jk>[4]</code> containing the specified characters.
7374    * @throws NumberFormatException If the number is negative.
7375    */
7376   public static char[] toHex4(int num) {
7377      if (num < 0)
7378         throw new NumberFormatException("toHex4 can only be used on non-negative numbers");
7379      var n = new char[4];
7380      var a = num % 16;
7381      n[3] = (char)(a > 9 ? 'A' + a - 10 : '0' + a);
7382      var base = 16;
7383      for (var i = 1; i < 4; i++) {
7384         a = (num / base) % 16;
7385         base <<= 4;
7386         n[3 - i] = (char)(a > 9 ? 'A' + a - 10 : '0' + a);
7387      }
7388      return n;
7389   }

7401      var n = new char[8];

7407         base <<= 4;
7408         n[7 - i] = (char)(a > 9 ? 'A' + a - 10 : '0' + a);
7409      }
7410      return n;
7411   }

7548   /**
7549    * Transliterates characters in a string by mapping characters from one set to another.
7550    *
7551    * <p>
7552    * Performs character-by-character translation. If a character is found in <c>fromChars</c>,
7553    * it is replaced with the corresponding character at the same position in <c>toChars</c>.
7554    * Characters not found in <c>fromChars</c> are left unchanged.
7555    *
7556    * <h5 class='section'>Example:</h5>
7557    * <p class='bjava'>
7558    *    transliterate(<js>"hello"</js>, <js>"aeiou"</js>, <js>"12345"</js>);
7559    *    <jc>// "h2ll4"</jc>
7560    *    transliterate(<js>"ABC"</js>, <js>"ABC"</js>, <js>"XYZ"</js>);
7561    *    <jc>// "XYZ"</jc>
7562    * </p>
7563    *
7564    * @param str The string to transliterate. Can be <jk>null</jk> (returns <jk>null</jk>).
7565    * @param fromChars The source character set. Can be <jk>null</jk> (returns <c>str</c> unchanged).
7566    * @param toChars The target character set. Can be <jk>null</jk> (returns <c>str</c> unchanged).
7567    * @return The transliterated string, or <jk>null</jk> if input is <jk>null</jk>.
7568    * @throws IllegalArgumentException If <c>fromChars</c> and <c>toChars</c> have different lengths.
7569    */
7570   public static String transliterate(String str, String fromChars, String toChars) {
7571      if (str == null)
7572         return null;
7573      if (fromChars == null || toChars == null || fromChars.isEmpty() || toChars.isEmpty())
7574         return str;
7575      if (fromChars.length() != toChars.length())
7576         throw iaex("fromChars and toChars must have the same length");
7577
7578      var sb = new StringBuilder(str.length());
7579      for (var i = 0; i < str.length(); i++) {
7580         var c = str.charAt(i);
7581         var index = fromChars.indexOf(c);
7582         if (index >= 0)
7583            sb.append(toChars.charAt(index));
7584         else
7585            sb.append(c);
7586      }
7587      return sb.toString();
7588   }

7715    * @param escaped The characters escaped.  Must not be <jk>null</jk> when the string is non-empty (a <jk>null</jk> argument throws {@link NullPointerException}).

7724            count++;

7726         return s;
7727      var sb = new StringBuffer(s.length() - count);
7728      for (var i = 0; i < s.length(); i++) {

7732            var c2 = s.charAt(i + 1);
7733            if (escaped.contains(c2)) {
7734               i++;
7735            }
7736         }
7737         sb.append(s.charAt(i));

7750    *   <li><js>"&amp;gt;"</js> → <js>'&gt;'</js></li>
7751    *   <li><js>"&amp;quot;"</js> → <js>'"'</js></li>
7752    *   <li><js>"&amp;#39;"</js> or <js>"&amp;apos;"</js> → <js>'\''</js></li>
7753    * </ul>
7754    *
7755    * <h5 class='section'>Example:</h5>
7756    * <p class='bjava'>
7757    *    unescapeHtml(<js>"&amp;lt;script&amp;gt;"</js>);     <jc>// Returns: "&lt;script&gt;"</jc>
7758    * </p>

7760    * @param str The string to unescape.
7761    * @return The unescaped string, or <jk>null</jk> if input is <jk>null</jk>.
7762    */

7767      return str.replace("&lt;", "<").replace("&gt;", ">").replace("&quot;", "\"").replace("&#39;", "'").replace("&apos;", "'").replace("&amp;", "&");

7920   /**

7934      for (var i = 0; i < s.length() && ! needsEncode; i++)
7935         needsEncode = URL_ENCODE_PATHINFO_VALIDCHARS.contains(s.charAt(i));
7936      if (! needsEncode)
7937         return s;

7940      var caw = new CharArrayWriter();
7941      var caseDiff = ('a' - 'A');
7942
7943      for (var i = 0; i < s.length();) {
7944         var c = s.charAt(i);
7945         if (URL_ENCODE_PATHINFO_VALIDCHARS.contains(c)) {
7946            sb.append(c);
7947            i++;
7948         } else {
7949            if (c == ' ') {
7950               sb.append('+');
7951               i++;
7952            } else {
7953               do {
7954                  caw.write(c);
7955                  if (c >= 0xD800 && c <= 0xDBFF && (i + 1) < s.length()) {
7956                     int d = s.charAt(i + 1);
7957                     if (d >= 0xDC00 && d <= 0xDFFF) {
7958                        caw.write(d);
7959                        i++;
7960                     }
7961                  }
7962                  i++;
7963                  if (i < s.length()) {
7964                     c = s.charAt(i);
7965                  }
7966               } while (i < s.length() && ! URL_ENCODE_PATHINFO_VALIDCHARS.contains(c));

7972                  sb.append('%');
7973                  var ch = forDigit((element >> 4) & 0xF, 16);
7974                  if (isLetter(ch)) {

7976                  }
7977                  sb.append(ch);
7978                  ch = forDigit(element & 0xF, 16);
7979                  if (isLetter(ch)) {
7980                     ch -= caseDiff;
7981                  }
7982                  sb.append(ch);
7983               }
7984               caw.reset();
7985            }
7986         }
7987      }
7988      return sb.toString();

7991   /**
7992    * Counts the number of words in a string.
7993    *
7994    * <p>
7995    * A word is defined as a sequence of one or more word characters (letters, digits, underscores)
7996    * separated by non-word characters.
7997    *
7998    * <h5 class='section'>Example:</h5>
7999    * <p class='bjava'>
8000    *    wordCount(<js>"Hello world"</js>);              <jc>// 2</jc>
8001    *    wordCount(<js>"The quick brown fox"</js>);      <jc>// 4</jc>
8002    *    wordCount(<js>"Hello, world! How are you?"</js>); <jc>// 5</jc>
8003    * </p>
8004    *
8005    * @param str The string to count words in. Can be <jk>null</jk>.
8006    * @return The number of words, or <c>0</c> if the string is <jk>null</jk> or empty.
8007    */
8008   public static int wordCount(String str) {
8009      if (isEmpty(str))
8010         return 0;
8011
8012      var count = 0;
8013      var inWord = false;
8014
8015      for (var i = 0; i < str.length(); i++) {
8016         var c = str.charAt(i);
8017         if ((LETTER.contains(c) || DIGIT.contains(c)) || c == '_') {
8018            if (! inWord) {
8019               count++;
8020               inWord = true;
8021            }
8022         } else {
8023            inWord = false;
8024         }
8025      }
8026
8027      return count;
8028   }

8030   /**

8032    *
8033    * <p>
8034    * Wraps text by breaking at word boundaries (spaces). Words longer than the wrap length
8035    * will be broken at the wrap length. Existing newlines are preserved.
8036    *
8037    * <h5 class='section'>Example:</h5>
8038    * <p class='bjava'>
8039    *    wrap(<js>"hello world test"</js>, 10);  <jc>// "hello world\ntest"</jc>
8040    *    wrap(<jk>null</jk>, 10);                <jc>// null</jc>
8041    * </p>
8042    *
8043    * @param str The string to wrap.
8044    * @param wrapLength The maximum line length (must be &gt; 0).
8045    * @return The wrapped string, or <jk>null</jk> if input is <jk>null</jk>.
8046    * @throws IllegalArgumentException if wrapLength is &lt;= 0.
8047    */

8052   /**
8053    * Wraps text to a specified line length with a custom newline string.
8054    *
8055    * <p>
8056    * Wraps text by breaking at word boundaries (spaces). Words longer than the wrap length
8057    * will be broken at the wrap length. Existing newlines are preserved.
8058    *
8059    * <h5 class='section'>Example:</h5>
8060    * <p class='bjava'>
8061    *    wrap(<js>"hello world test"</js>, 10, <js>"<br>"</js>);  <jc>// "hello world<br>test"</jc>
8062    *    wrap(<jk>null</jk>, 10, <js>"\n"</js>);                  <jc>// null</jc>
8063    * </p>
8064    *
8065    * @param str The string to wrap.
8066    * @param wrapLength The maximum line length (must be &gt; 0).
8067    * @param newline The string to use as line separator.
8068    * @return The wrapped string, or <jk>null</jk> if input is <jk>null</jk>.
8069    * @throws IllegalArgumentException if wrapLength is &lt;= 0 or newline is <jk>null</jk>.
8070    */
8071   public static String wrap(String str, int wrapLength, String newline) {
8072      if (str == null)
8073         return null;
8074      if (isEmpty(str))
8075         return str;
8076      if (wrapLength <= 0)
8077         throw iaex("wrapLength must be > 0: %s", wrapLength);
8078      if (newline == null)
8079         throw iaex("newline cannot be null");
8080
8081      var result = new StringBuilder();
8082      var lines = str.split("\r?\n", -1);  // Preserve empty lines
8083
8084      for (var lineIdx = 0; lineIdx < lines.length; lineIdx++) {
8085         var line = lines[lineIdx];
8086         if (line.isEmpty()) {
8087            if (lineIdx < lines.length - 1)
8088               result.append(newline);
8089            continue;
8090         }
8091
8092         // Split into words first, then combine words that fit
8093         var words = line.split(" +");  // Split on one or more spaces
8094         var currentLine = new StringBuilder();
8095
8096         for (var word : words) {
8097            if (word.isEmpty())
8098               continue;
8099
8100            var wordLength = word.length();
8101            var currentLength = currentLine.length();
8102
8103            if (currentLength == 0) {
8104               // First word on line
8105               // Only break single words if there are multiple words in the input
8106               // (single long words should not be broken for readability)
8107               if (wordLength > wrapLength && words.length > 1) {
8108                  // Word is too long and there are other words, break it
8109                  if (!result.isEmpty())
8110                     result.append(newline);
8111                  var wordPos = 0;
8112                  while (wordPos < wordLength) {
8113                     if (wordPos > 0)
8114                        result.append(newline);
8115                     var remaining = wordLength - wordPos;
8116                     if (remaining <= wrapLength) {
8117                        result.append(word.substring(wordPos));
8118                        break;
8119                     }
8120                     result.append(word.substring(wordPos, wordPos + wrapLength));
8121                     wordPos += wrapLength;
8122                  }
8123               } else {
8124                  currentLine.append(word);
8125               }
8126            } else {
8127               // Check if we can add this word to current line
8128               var neededLength = currentLength + 1 + wordLength;  // current + space + word
8129               // Break if it would fit exactly or exceed - prefer breaking for readability
8130               if (neededLength < wrapLength) {
8131                  // Fits with room to spare
8132                  currentLine.append(' ').append(word);
8133               } else {
8134                  // Doesn't fit or fits exactly - start new line
8135                  if (!result.isEmpty())
8136                     result.append(newline);
8137                  result.append(currentLine);
8138                  currentLine.setLength(0);
8139                  if (wordLength > wrapLength && words.length > 1) {
8140                     // Word is too long and there are other words, break it
8141                     result.append(newline);
8142                     var wordPos = 0;
8143                     while (wordPos < wordLength) {
8144                        if (wordPos > 0)
8145                           result.append(newline);
8146                        var remaining = wordLength - wordPos;
8147                        if (remaining <= wrapLength) {
8148                           result.append(word.substring(wordPos));
8149                           break;
8150                        }
8151                        result.append(word.substring(wordPos, wordPos + wrapLength));
8152                        wordPos += wrapLength;
8153                     }
8154                  } else {
8155                     currentLine.append(word);
8156                  }
8157               }
8158            }
8159         }
8160
8161         // Append any remaining line
8162         if (!currentLine.isEmpty()) {
8163            if (!result.isEmpty())
8164               result.append(newline);
8165            result.append(currentLine);
8166         }
8167      }
8168
8169      return result.toString();
8170   }

8172   /**
8173    * Helper method to estimate the number of syllables in a word.
8174    */
8175   private static int estimateSyllables(String word) {
8176
8177      var lower = word.toLowerCase(Locale.ROOT);
8178      var count = 0;
8179      var prevWasVowel = false;
8180
8181      for (var i = 0; i < lower.length(); i++) {
8182         var c = lower.charAt(i);
8183         var isVowel = (VOWEL.contains(c) || c == 'y');
8184
8185         if (isVowel && ! prevWasVowel) {
8186            count++;
8187         }
8188         prevWasVowel = isVowel;
8189      }
8190
8191      // Handle silent 'e' at the end
8192      if (lower.endsWith("e") && count > 1) {
8193         count--;
8194      }
8195
8196      // At least one syllable
8197      return Math.max(1, count);
8198   }

8200   /**
8201    * Finds the first non-whitespace, non-comment character in a string.
8202    *
8203    * @param s The string to analyze.
8204    * @return The first real character, or <c>-1</c> if none found.
8205    */
8206   private static int firstRealCharacter(String s) {
8207      return safe(()-> {
8208         var r = new StringReader(s);
8209         var c = 0;
8210         while ((c = r.read()) != -1) {
8211            if (! isWhitespace(c)) {
8212               if (c == '/') {
8213                  skipComments(r);
8214               } else {
8215                  return c;
8216               }
8217            }
8218         }
8219         return -1;
8220      });
8221   }

8223   /**
8224    * Helper method to get Soundex code for a character.
8225    */
8226   private static char getSoundexCode(char c) {
8227      if (c == 'A' || c == 'E' || c == 'I' || c == 'O' || c == 'U' || c == 'H' || c == 'W' || c == 'Y')
8228         return '0';
8229      if (c == 'B' || c == 'F' || c == 'P' || c == 'V')
8230         return '1';
8231      if (c == 'C' || c == 'G' || c == 'J' || c == 'K' || c == 'Q' || c == 'S' || c == 'X' || c == 'Z')
8232         return '2';
8233      if (c == 'D' || c == 'T')
8234         return '3';
8235      if (c == 'L')
8236         return '4';
8237      if (c == 'M' || c == 'N')
8238         return '5';
8239      if (c == 'R')
8240         return '6';
8241      return '0'; // Non-letter characters
8242   }

8244   /**
8245    * Validates if a string is a valid IPv6 address format (without network operations).
8246    *
8247    * <p>
8248    * This method performs pure string-based validation and does not perform any DNS lookups
8249    * or network operations, making it fast and suitable for validation purposes.
8250    *
8251    * @param ip The IPv6 address string to validate.
8252    * @return <jk>true</jk> if the string is a valid IPv6 address format, <jk>false</jk> otherwise.
8253    */
8254   @SuppressWarnings({
8255      "java:S1313" // IPv6 validation intentionally compares against canonical literals like :: and ::ffff
8256   })
8257   public static boolean isValidIPv6Address(String ip) {
8258      if (ip == null || ip.isEmpty())
8259         return false;
8260
8261      // IPv6 addresses can be:
8262      // 1. Full format: 2001:0db8:85a3:0000:0000:8a2e:0370:7334 (8 groups of 4 hex digits)
8263      // 2. Compressed format: 2001:db8::1 (uses :: to represent consecutive zeros)
8264      // 3. IPv4-mapped: ::ffff:192.168.1.1 (last 32 bits as IPv4)
8265      // 4. Loopback: ::1
8266      // 5. Unspecified: ::
8267
8268      // Cannot start or end with a single colon (except ::)
8269      if (ip.startsWith(":") && !ip.startsWith("::"))
8270         return false;
8271      if (ip.endsWith(":") && !ip.endsWith("::"))
8272         return false;
8273
8274      // Check for IPv4-mapped format (contains both : and .)
8275      if (ip.contains(".")) {
8276         // Must be in format ::ffff:x.x.x.x or similar
8277         var lastColon = ip.lastIndexOf(":");
8278         if (lastColon < 0)
8279            return false;
8280         var ipv4Part = ip.substring(lastColon + 1);
8281         // Validate IPv4 part
8282         var ipv4Parts = ipv4Part.split("\\.");
8283         if (ipv4Parts.length != 4)
8284            return false;
8285         for (var part : ipv4Parts) {
8286            try {
8287               var num = Integer.parseInt(part);
8288               if (num < 0 || num > 255)
8289                  return false;
8290            } catch (@SuppressWarnings("unused") NumberFormatException e) {
8291               return false;
8292            }
8293         }
8294         // Validate IPv6 part before the IPv4
8295         var ipv6Part = ip.substring(0, lastColon);
8296         // Accept empty, ::, ::ffff, ::FFFF, or : (when string starts with ::)
8297         if (ipv6Part.isEmpty() || ipv6Part.equals("::") || ipv6Part.equals("::ffff") || ipv6Part.equals("::FFFF") || (ipv6Part.equals(":") && ip.startsWith("::")))
8298            return true;
8299         // More complex validation would be needed for other IPv4-mapped formats
8300         // For now, accept common formats
8301      }
8302
8303      // Check for :: (compression) - only one allowed
8304      var doubleColonCount = 0;
8305      for (var i = 1; i < ip.length(); i++) {
8306         if (ip.charAt(i) == ':' && ip.charAt(i - 1) == ':') {
8307            doubleColonCount++;
8308            if (doubleColonCount > 1)
8309               return false; // Only one :: allowed
8310         }
8311      }
8312
8313      // Split by ::
8314      var parts = ip.split("::", -1);
8315
8316      if (parts.length == 2) {
8317         // Compressed format
8318         var leftParts = parts[0].isEmpty() ? new String[0] : parts[0].split(":");
8319         var rightParts = parts[1].isEmpty() ? new String[0] : parts[1].split(":");
8320         var totalParts = leftParts.length + rightParts.length;
8321         if (totalParts > 7)
8322            return false; // Too many groups (max 8, but :: counts as one or more)
8323      } else {
8324         // Full format (no compression)
8325         var groups = ip.split(":");
8326         if (groups.length != 8)
8327            return false;
8328      }
8329
8330      // Validate each hex group
8331      var groups = ip.split("::");
8332      for (var groupSection : groups) {
8333         if (groupSection.isEmpty())
8334            continue; // Skip empty section from ::
8335         var groupParts = groupSection.split(":");
8336         for (var group : groupParts) {
8337            if (group.length() > 4)
8338               return false; // Each group is max 4 hex digits
8339            // Validate hex digits
8340            for (var i = 0; i < group.length(); i++) {
8341               var c = group.charAt(i);
8342               if (! HEXADECIMAL_CHARS.contains(c))
8343                  return false;
8344            }
8345         }
8346      }
8347
8348      return true;
8349   }

8352   private static class Readifier {
8353      private final Class<?> type;
8354      private final Function<Object,String> bridge;
8355
8356      private <T> Readifier(Class<T> type, Function<? super T,String> converter) {
8357         this.type = type;
8358         this.bridge = o -> converter.apply(type.cast(o));
8359      }
8360
8361      Class<?> forClass() {
8362         return type;
8363      }
8364
8365      Function<Object,String> toFunction() {
8366         return bridge;
8367      }
8368   }

8370   private static <T> Readifier readifier(Class<T> type, Function<? super T,String> converter) {
8371      return new Readifier(type, converter);
8372   }
