8374   private static List<Readifier> loadReadifiers() {
8375      var list = new ArrayList<Readifier>();
8376
8377      // More specific types first - order matters!
8378      list.add(readifier(Map.Entry.class, x -> readable(x.getKey()) + '=' + readable(x.getValue())));
8379      list.add(readifier(Collection.class, x -> ((Collection<?>)x).stream().map(StringUtils::readable).collect(joining(",", "[", "]"))));
8380      list.add(readifier(Map.class, x -> ((Map<?,?>)x).entrySet().stream().map(StringUtils::readable).collect(joining(",", "{", "}"))));
8381      list.add(readifier(Iterable.class, x -> readable(toList(x))));
8382      list.add(readifier(Iterator.class, x -> readable(toList(x))));
8383      list.add(readifier(Enumeration.class, x -> readable(toList(x))));
8384      list.add(readifier(Optional.class, x -> readable(((Optional<?>)x).orElse(null))));
8385      list.add(readifier(GregorianCalendar.class, x -> x.toZonedDateTime().format(DateTimeFormatter.ISO_INSTANT)));
8386      list.add(readifier(Date.class, x -> x.toInstant().toString()));
8387      list.add(readifier(InputStream.class, x -> toHex(x)));
8388      list.add(readifier(Reader.class, (Reader x) -> safe(() -> read(x))));
8389      list.add(readifier(File.class, (File x) -> safe(() -> read(x))));
8390      list.add(readifier(byte[].class, x -> toHex(x)));
8391      list.add(readifier(Enum.class, x -> ((Enum<?>)x).name()));
8392      list.add(readifier(Class.class, ClassUtils::classNameSimple));
8393      list.add(readifier(Constructor.class, x -> ConstructorInfo.of(x).getNameFull()));
8394      list.add(readifier(Method.class, x -> MethodInfo.of(x).getNameFull()));
8395      list.add(readifier(Field.class, x -> FieldInfo.of(x).toString()));
8396      list.add(readifier(Parameter.class, x -> ParameterInfo.of(x).toString()));
8397      list.add(readifier(ClassInfo.class, ClassInfo::toString));
8398      list.add(readifier(MethodInfo.class, MethodInfo::toString));
8399      list.add(readifier(ConstructorInfo.class, ConstructorInfo::toString));
8400      list.add(readifier(FieldInfo.class, FieldInfo::toString));
8401      list.add(readifier(ParameterInfo.class, ParameterInfo::toString));
8402
8403      return Collections.unmodifiableList(list);
8404   }

8406   /**
8407    * Determines the multiplier value based on the suffix character in a string.
8408    *
8409    * @param s The string to analyze for multiplier suffix.
8410    * @return The multiplier value (1 if no valid suffix found).
8411    */
8412   private static int multiplierInt(String s) {
8413      var c = isEmpty(s) ? 'z' : s.charAt(s.length() - 1);
8414      if (c == 'G')
8415         return 1024 * 1024 * 1024;
8416      if (c == 'M')
8417         return 1024 * 1024;
8418      if (c == 'K')
8419         return 1024;
8420      if (c == 'g')
8421         return 1000 * 1000 * 1000;
8422      if (c == 'm')
8423         return 1000 * 1000;
8424      if (c == 'k')
8425         return 1000;
8426      return 1;
8427   }
8428
8429   /**
8430    * Determines the long multiplier value based on the suffix character in a string.
8431    *
8432    * @param s The string to analyze for multiplier suffix.
8433    * @return The multiplier value (1 if no valid suffix found).
8434    */
8435   private static long multiplierLong(String s) {
8436      if (isEmpty(s))
8437         return 1;
8438      var c = s.charAt(s.length() - 1);
8439      if (c == 'P')
8440         return 1125899906842624L;  // 1024^5
8441      if (c == 'T')
8442         return 1099511627776L;  // 1024^4
8443      if (c == 'G')
8444         return 1073741824L;  // 1024^3
8445      if (c == 'M')
8446         return 1048576L;  // 1024^2
8447      if (c == 'K')
8448         return 1024L;
8449      if (c == 'p')
8450         return 1000000000000000L;  // 1000^5
8451      if (c == 't')
8452         return 1000000000000L;  // 1000^4
8453      if (c == 'g')
8454         return 1000000000L;  // 1000^3
8455      if (c == 'm')
8456         return 1000000L;  // 1000^2
8457      if (c == 'k')
8458         return 1000L;
8459      return 1;
8460   }

8462   /**
8463    * Parses a unit string and converts the value to milliseconds.
8464    *
8465    * @param unit The unit string (case-insensitive, already lowercased).
8466    * @param value The numeric value.
8467    * @return The value in milliseconds, or <c>-1</c> if the unit is invalid.
8468    */
8469   private static long parseUnit(String unit, double value) {
8470      if (isEmpty(unit)) {
8471         // No unit means milliseconds
8472         return (long)value;
8473      }
8474
8475      // Check milliseconds first (before minutes) - must check exact "ms" before checking "m"
8476      if (unit.equals("ms") || unit.equals("millis") || unit.equals("milliseconds"))
8477         return (long)value;
8478
8479      // Seconds
8480      if (unit.startsWith("s") && !unit.startsWith("sec"))
8481         return (long)(value * 1000);
8482      if (unit.startsWith("sec") || unit.startsWith("second"))
8483         return (long)(value * 1000);
8484
8485      // Minutes (must check after milliseconds and months)
8486      if (unit.startsWith("m") && !unit.startsWith("mo") && !unit.startsWith("mill") && !unit.startsWith("ms"))
8487         return (long)(value * 1000 * 60);
8488      if (unit.startsWith("min") || unit.startsWith("minute"))
8489         return (long)(value * 1000 * 60);
8490
8491      // Hours
8492      if (unit.startsWith("h") || unit.startsWith("hour"))
8493         return (long)(value * 1000 * 60 * 60);
8494
8495      // Days
8496      if (unit.startsWith("d") && !unit.startsWith("da"))
8497         return (long)(value * 1000 * 60 * 60 * 24);
8498      if (unit.startsWith("day"))
8499         return (long)(value * 1000 * 60 * 60 * 24);
8500
8501      // Weeks
8502      if (unit.startsWith("w") || unit.startsWith("week"))
8503         return (long)(value * 1000 * 60 * 60 * 24 * 7);
8504
8505      // Months (30 days)
8506      if (unit.startsWith("mo") || unit.startsWith("month"))
8507         return (long)(value * 1000 * 60 * 60 * 24 * 30);
8508
8509      // Years (365 days)
8510      if (unit.startsWith("y") && !unit.startsWith("yr"))
8511         return (long)(value * 1000 * 60 * 60 * 24 * 365);
8512      if (unit.startsWith("yr") || unit.startsWith("year"))
8513         return (long)(value * 1000 * 60 * 60 * 24 * 365);
8514
8515      // Unknown unit
8516      return -1;
8517   }

8519   /**
8520    * Skips over a single comment sequence in a StringReader.
8521    *
8522    * <p>
8523    * The reader must be positioned at the first <js>'/'</js> character of a comment.
8524    * This method will skip only the comment it's currently positioned on, not all comments in the reader.
8525    *
8526    * <p>
8527    * Supports both <js>"/* * /"</js> style block comments and <js>"//"</js> style line comments.
8528    *
8529    * @param r The StringReader positioned at the start of a comment (at the first <js>'/'</js>).  Must not be <jk>null</jk> (a <jk>null</jk> argument throws {@link NullPointerException}).
8530    * @throws IOException If an I/O error occurs.
8531    */
8532   public static void skipComments(StringReader r) throws IOException {
8533      var c = r.read();
8534      //  "/* */" style comments
8535      if (c == '*') {
8536         c = r.read();
8537         while (c != -1) {
8538            if (c == '*') {
8539               c = r.read();
8540               if (c == '/')
8541                  return;
8542               // If not '/', continue checking from this character
8543               // Don't read again, just continue the loop
8544            } else {
8545               c = r.read();
8546            }
8547         }
8548         //  "//" style comments
8549      } else if (c == '/') {
8550         while ((c = r.read()) != -1) {
8551            if (c == '\n')
8552               return;
8553         }
8554      }
8555   }

8562    */
8563   private static AsciiSet getEscapeSet(char c) {
8564      return ESCAPE_SETS.computeIfAbsent(c, key -> AsciiSet.create().chars(key, '\\').build());

8567   /**
8568    * Helper method to split a string into words.
8569    * Detects word boundaries from separators (spaces, underscores, hyphens) and case changes.
8570    *
8571    * @param str The string to split.
8572    * @return A list of words, or empty list if input is null or empty.
8573    */
8574   private static List<String> splitWords(String str) {
8575      if (str == null || isEmpty(str))
8576         return Collections.emptyList();
8577
8578      var words = new ArrayList<String>();
8579      var sb = new StringBuilder();
8580      var wasLowerCase = false;
8581      var wasUpperCase = false;
8582      var consecutiveUpperCount = 0;
8583
8584      for (var i = 0; i < str.length(); i++) {
8585         var c = str.charAt(i);
8586         var isSeparator = (c == ' ' || c == '_' || c == '-' || c == '\t');
8587         var isUpperCase = LETTER_UC.contains(c);
8588         var isLowerCase = LETTER_LC.contains(c);
8589         var isLetter = LETTER.contains(c);
8590
8591         if (isSeparator) {
8592            if (!sb.isEmpty()) {
8593               words.add(sb.toString());
8594               sb.setLength(0);
8595            }
8596            wasLowerCase = false;
8597            wasUpperCase = false;
8598            consecutiveUpperCount = 0;
8599         } else if (isLetter) {
8600            // Detect word boundary:
8601            // 1. Uppercase after lowercase (e.g., "helloWorld" → "hello", "World")
8602            // 2. Uppercase after consecutive uppercase when next is lowercase (e.g., "XMLHttp" → "XML", "Http")
8603            // 3. Lowercase after 2+ consecutive uppercase (e.g., "XMLHttp" → "XML", "Http")
8604            if (!sb.isEmpty()) {
8605               if (isUpperCase && wasLowerCase) {
8606                  // Case 1: uppercase after lowercase (e.g., "helloWorld" → "hello", "World")
8607                  words.add(sb.toString());
8608                  sb.setLength(0);
8609                  consecutiveUpperCount = 0;
8610               } else if (isUpperCase && wasUpperCase && consecutiveUpperCount >= 2) {
8611                  // Case 2: uppercase after uppercase - check if this starts a new word
8612                  // Look ahead to see if next character is lowercase
8613                  // This handles "XMLHttp" where 'H' starts "Http"
8614                  // We need at least 2 consecutive uppercase letters before this one to split
8615                  if (i + 1 < str.length()) {
8616                     var nextChar = str.charAt(i + 1);
8617                     if (LETTER_LC.contains(nextChar)) {
8618                        // This uppercase starts a new word, split before it
8619                        words.add(sb.toString());
8620                        sb.setLength(0);
8621                        consecutiveUpperCount = 0;
8622                     }
8623                  }
8624               } else if (isLowerCase && wasUpperCase && consecutiveUpperCount >= 2) {
8625                  // Case 3: lowercase after 2+ consecutive uppercase
8626                  // Split all but the last uppercase (e.g., "XMLH" → "XML" + "H")
8627                  var splitPoint = sb.length() - 1;
8628                  words.add(sb.substring(0, splitPoint));
8629                  sb.delete(0, splitPoint);
8630                  consecutiveUpperCount = 0;
8631               }
8632            }
8633            sb.append(c);
8634            // Update state AFTER appending
8635            wasLowerCase = isLowerCase;
8636            wasUpperCase = isUpperCase;
8637            if (isUpperCase) {
8638               consecutiveUpperCount++;
8639            } else {
8640               consecutiveUpperCount = 0;
8641            }
8642         } else {
8643            // Non-letter characters (digits, etc.) - treat as part of current word
8644            sb.append(c);
8645            wasLowerCase = false;
8646            wasUpperCase = false;
8647         consecutiveUpperCount = 0;
8648      }
8649   }
8650
8651   if (!sb.isEmpty())
8652      words.add(sb.toString());
8653
8654      return words;
8655   }

8663    */

8690   /**
8691    * Creates a new {@link StringBuilder} with the stringified form of each specified value appended in order.
8692    *
8693    * <p>
8694    * Each value is rendered via {@link ObjectUtils#stringify(Object)} (a <jk>null</jk> value renders as
8695    * the literal string {@code "null"}). With no arguments, an empty builder is returned.
8696    *
8697    * @param values The values to append in order. Individual values can be <jk>null</jk>.
8698    * @return A new StringBuilder containing the appended values.
8699    */
8700   public static StringBuilder newStringBuilder(Object...values) {
8701      var b = new StringBuilder();
8702      for (var v : values)
8703         b.append(stringify(v));
8704      return b;
8705   }

8707   /**
8708    * Inverse of {@link #equalsIgnoreCase(String, String)}.
8709    *
8710    * @param s1 String 1.
8711    * @param s2 String 2.
8712    * @return <jk>true</jk> if the strings are not equal ignoring case.
8713    */
8714   public static boolean notEqualsIgnoreCase(String s1, String s2) { return ! equalsIgnoreCase(s1, s2); }

8716   /**
8717    * Returns the specified string, or <jk>null</jk> if that string is <jk>null</jk> or empty.
8718    *
8719    * @param value The string value to check.
8720    * @return The string value, or <jk>null</jk> if the string is <jk>null</jk> or empty.
8721    */
8722   public static String nullIfEmpty(String value) {
8723      return isEmpty(value) ? null : value;
8724   }
